dedupe_keys.name: ovhcloud strasbourg data centre fire of 10 march 2021 bea ri investigation

description: This post-event analysis is the safety investigation report (No. MTE-BEARI-2022-005, dated 24 May 2022, 43 pages) of the French industrial-risk investigation office BEA-RI into the fire that destroyed the SBG2 data centre of OVHcloud in Strasbourg on 10 March 2021 and damaged neighbouring buildings. The fire started in the energy rooms housing the uninterruptible power supply equipment and lead batteries that served the servers; these rooms had fire detection but no automatic extinguishing system, and fire broke out almost simultaneously on batteries and on an inverter. The report describes how the building's design with free-air cooling, the lack of automatic extinguishing, the delay in cutting electrical supply and limited water resources allowed the fire to spread through SBG2 and to adjacent buildings despite a fast fire-service response; there were no casualties, but material damage was large and service stopped for many customers, including public bodies, some of whom lost data without off-site backups. The BEA-RI does not state the precise cause, which was subject to a judicial expert inquiry, and issues safety lessons and recommendations on battery and charging rooms, detection, extinguishing and electrical isolation. Coverage: one site in France. Format and access: free PDF; the official report is in French and an English machine translation circulates. Caveats: cause undetermined; the translated copy is unofficial. Simulation uses: hazard exposure and cascading failure in data centres, business continuity and disaster recovery planning. Related records: Uptime Institute outage analyses and the EU data centre energy reporting provide wider context.

outcomes: The BEA-RI found that the lack of automatic extinguishing, delayed electrical isolation and the building design let the fire spread, and recommended treating battery charging equipment rooms as fire-risk rooms with detection and extinguishing.
